name: Cotton
description: Cotton is Gujarat's leading cash crop. Sucking pests in the early stage and bollworms from square formation onward decide most of the yield, so timely, rotated sprays and balanced nutrition at flowering make the biggest difference.
tips: Scout twice a week from 20 days after sowing; spray sucking-pest products only when pest counts cross the economic threshold.
Rotate insecticides with different modes of action between sprays to slow resistance, especially for whitefly and pink bollworm.
Use pheromone traps to monitor pink bollworm and destroy rosette flowers early in the season.
Always read the product label for the registered dose and waiting period before harvest.

name: Groundnut
description: Groundnut is a key kharif oilseed for Saurashtra and Kutch. Early weed control, protection from soil pests like white grub, and preventing tikka leaf spot keep pods well filled and oil content high.

solutions.name: Thioseed
solutions.type: Seed treatment for early sucking pests — Thiamethoxam 30% FS

solutions.name: Hitachi
solutions.type: Grassy & broad-leaf weeds — Quizalofop Ethyl 7.5% + Imazethapyr 15% EC

solutions.name: Tropister
solutions.type: Tikka leaf spot — Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC

solutions.name: Shaan
solutions.type: Collar rot & leaf spot — Carbendazim 12% + Mancozeb 63% WP

tips: Treat seed before sowing to protect seedlings from soil-borne diseases and early pests.
Keep the field weed-free for the first 45 days; weeds compete hardest before pegging.
Apply gypsum at pegging for better pod filling, and avoid disturbing the soil once pegs enter it.
Always read the product label for the registered dose and waiting period before harvest.

name: Cumin
description: Cumin (jeera) is a high-value rabi spice for North Gujarat. It is very sensitive to blight and powdery mildew in cloudy, humid weather, so protective sprays at the right time protect both yield and seed colour.
tips: Start protective blight sprays when the crop is 30–35 days old, and repeat after cloudy or foggy spells.
Avoid excess irrigation and nitrogen; lush, wet crops are far more prone to blight.
Follow a crop rotation and avoid sowing cumin in the same field every year to reduce wilt.
Always read the product label for the registered dose and waiting period before harvest.

name: Chilli
description: Chilli needs protection across a long season — thrips and mites curl the leaves, fruit borers damage the pods, and anthracnose (die-back) causes fruit rot. Balanced nutrition reduces flower and fruit drop.

solutions.name: Meta Max Gold
solutions.type: Damping off in nursery — Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP

solutions.name: Flo Fix
solutions.type: Flower & fruit drop — Alpha Naphthyl Acetic Acid 4.5% SL

tips: Raise seedlings in raised nursery beds and treat the nursery against damping off.
Use blue or yellow sticky traps to monitor thrips and whitefly from transplanting.
Pick and destroy fruits showing borer damage or anthracnose spots to reduce spread.
Always read the product label for the registered dose and waiting period before harvest.

name: Onion
description: Onion is grown in both kharif and rabi. Thrips and purple blotch are the major threats to bulb size, and early weed control is critical because the crop's narrow leaves compete poorly.

solutions.name: Tropister
solutions.type: Purple blotch & Stemphylium — Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC

solutions.name: Goodfix
solutions.type: Better spray coverage on waxy leaves — silicon spreader

tips: Add a spreader to every spray — onion leaves are waxy and sprays run off without one.
Stop irrigation 10–15 days before harvest for better bulb storage life.
Cure bulbs in shade for a week before storage to reduce rotting.
Always read the product label for the registered dose and waiting period before harvest.

name: Garlic
description: Garlic is a long-duration rabi crop. Thrips, purple blotch and weeds are the main yield reducers, and steady potassium supply improves clove size and storage quality.

solutions.name: Tropister
solutions.type: Purple blotch & Stemphylium — Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC

tips: Plant healthy, medium-to-large cloves; small cloves give small bulbs.
Keep the field weed-free during the first 60 days of growth.
Harvest when the tops yellow and bend over, then cure the bulbs in shade.
Always read the product label for the registered dose and waiting period before harvest.

name: Tomato
description: Tomato is affected by fruit borer and leaf miner above ground and by early and late blight in humid weather. Whitefly spreads leaf curl virus, so early vector control and regular protective sprays are essential.

solutions.name: Meta Max Gold
solutions.type: Damping off in nursery — Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP

tips: Grow nursery under insect-proof net to keep whitefly — and leaf curl virus — away from seedlings.
Remove and destroy virus-infected plants early to stop the disease spreading.
Stake plants and prune lower leaves to improve airflow and reduce blight.
Always read the product label for the registered dose and waiting period before harvest.

name: Coriander
description: Coriander is grown for both leaves and seed. Powdery mildew and aphids are the main problems during flowering, and wilt can appear in fields where the crop is repeated.
tips: Sow treated seed and avoid waterlogging to keep wilt in check.
Watch for aphids as flowering begins — that is when populations build fastest.
For leaf harvest, keep a gap between the last spray and cutting as stated on the label.
Always read the product label for the registered dose and waiting period before harvest.
